angle: A veteran pastor's read on a man who feeds everyone and is fed by no one. He opens the app at 6am with Sunday already leaning on him. Two things are true at once — he needs God, and he needs a sermon — and the app currently makes him meet them in the wrong order: the greeting says "not ministry, just you and God" and the very next card is a work errand that throws him out of the app. My whole design is about the order those two things arrive in, and about never letting the work disappear while it waits its turn.
thesis: His own reading comes first, his work comes second and is never more than one tap away, and the app never pretends to be his ghostwriter. Everything else — trust lines, the filed bag, the quiet door — follows from that order.
principles: Feed the man before you serve the pastor. The reading and Between You & God sit above anything that leaves the app for Sunday (rulings: Sermon Notes row demoted below the reading for pastor_leader; PR #82 put Between You & God directly beneath the reading).
Never take the work away, only move it down. He came for a sermon too. Preach stays on Home, one tap, with a count of what is waiting.
The AI thinks with him; it does not write for him and it does not quote what it has not checked. 79% of pastors worry AI could replace God's role, 63% pastoral leadership (Barna/Gloo, Dec 2025).

Show the source, always, on the surface. Reviewers document AI tools fabricating cross-references on less-common passages; the study layer is already public-domain and CC, so make the licence visible rather than buried in Settings.
Presence over problem-solving. Between You & God asks; it does not diagnose, prescribe or graduate him.
Never fabricate a number. Campus Overview shows real analytics or a code prompt, and 'time saved' becomes 'what you gathered', because we can count captures and we cannot count minutes.
Nothing on this path shames him. No streak threat, no 'you missed a day', no notification that implies he let God down.
Crisis is not a persona anyone picks on a good day — least of all a pastor. Comfort must be reachable from his path without changing his path.

journey.day0: He arrives one of two ways. Either he taps the path swatch or the landing line and picks 'I'm a pastor and I teach and preach' in the one sheet, which saves as a real choice and navigates straight to Home (PR #89/#93 rulings); or he signs in with his work email in More and the boot restore stamps pastor_leader (only when dw_setup is absent or auto-sourced) and provisions his campus code. Home opens with today's chapter already open, credit-free, commentary expanded, Between You & God under it. The arrival strip names where he is and points at what is open. With no plan yet the hero serves the PASTOR_CHAPTERS leadership rotation so the screen is never blank, with one line saying what the rotation is and that a dated plan is a tap away.
journey.first_session: He reads. He is not asked for anything. Under the reading, Between You & God asks him one question about himself, not about his staff, with Journal this / Talk it through and a line telling him nobody at the church can read it. Below that, commentary with its source printed. Below that, the study assistant with its four prompts and one honest line about what it will and will not do. Below that, Preach — the only thing that leaves the app, and it now sits under his own reading rather than over it. If he highlights a verse, To sermon files it; the Preach card's second line changes to name the count. No push ask, no email ask, nothing until he has finished a reading (the existing evidence-timed gate stack).
journey.return_visit: Same screen, same order, nothing re-explained. If he started a plan, Today's Study replaces the rotation and the Greek/Hebrew toggle is on the passage. The Preach card carries the running count of what he has filed; tapping the count opens the filed sheet, where he can copy it all out, edit what he is preaching through, and remove anything. The reflection prompt has rotated. Streak is in the greeting, never as a warning.
journey.week2: He has a rhythm or he does not, and the app treats both the same. His filed bag has real weight now, which is the moment the export step earns itself — copy all, or hand across to Pastors Sermon Prep. On Sunday, Your week appears with two tiles, one true line about what he gathered, and one question written for a pastor rather than a congregant. He has probably found the study assistant's Greek prompt and the source line; if the trust work lands, session length goes up and the event will say so.
journey.missed_day: Nothing changes on screen except the streak number. The existing single freeze bridges one missed day and never announces itself. He gets no catch-up prompt, no 'you were doing so well', no re-onboarding. Guilt-framed streak reminders drive notification opt-out and uninstall, and a pastor already carries a professional obligation to be devout — the app must not add to it. If more than one day is missed, the count resets quietly and the greeting drops back to 'This is your time — not ministry, just you and God', which is the right sentence for the day he comes back.
journey.seasonal: Advent, Lent, Easter and a Futures series are the spikes (YouVersion 21.6M opens on Easter 2026; Hallow's 300% Lent growth). For every other persona the seasonal read is something they join. For the pastor it is something he starts for his campus, and the estate already has the mechanism: /staff intake, which he uses and which has an approval chain. For the first two weeks he sees only the reader's side — a plan he can start. Whether a campus pastor can launch a campus-wide read from inside Daily Word is an owner decision, not something to build into this pass.

comfort_access: One quiet line at the foot of pastor Home — "Comfort readings — scripture only, nothing asked." — plus the same entry from Bible AI's empty state. It opens the comfort surface as a sub-view over his own path: his saved persona is never touched, closing returns him to pastor Home, the toolbar is Note and Close only, and there is no graduation prompt, no streak, no count and no completion. It is worded as a place, not a condition, because a check-in question is exactly what a pastor will refuse. Separately, if crisis language appears in what he types into Bible AI or a prayer request, the safety panel takes over the answer area: presence first, then the region-correct line matched to his campus, then the disclosure that this is scripture and a church rather than counselling, then Keep reading / I'm okay. It never stacks with another gate and never re-triggers in the same session for the same message. The keyword matcher needs a false-positive suite before it ships — "the death of Christ" and "I'm dying to preach this" must not fire; "I don't want to be here any more" must.
reminders: One a day, at the hour he actually opens, worded neutrally, and never about the streak. The machinery already exists — a stored preferred_hour per subscriber, an hourly cron with a two-hour catch-up window and a once-per-local-day ledger — so this is a copy and timing change, not new plumbing. Replace the streak-flavoured templates for this persona with the reading itself: "Your chapter is open. 1 Peter 5." or "Ten minutes before the day starts." Never "don't lose your streak", never "you missed yesterday". Guilt-framed reminders drive opt-out and uninstall, and a pastor already carries a professional obligation to be devout; the app must not add to it. The ask itself stays where it is — after his first finished reading, never stacked with the path question. Two pastor-specific questions are his to settle: whether push is suppressed Sunday morning while he is working, and whether the inferred-time logic should ignore Sunday opens entirely when learning his hour. Both are plausible and unsourced, so they should be shipped as switches and tested rather than assumed.
instrumentation: pastor_home_open — detail: plan | rotation | read_today. The denominator for everything else, and the only way to know whether the rotation floor holds a pastor who has not started a plan.

pastor_reflection_shown / pastor_reflection_journal / pastor_reflection_talk — detail carries the prompt index and whether it is a man-facing or ministry-facing prompt. This is the A/B that proves or kills the prompt rewrite.

pastor_prompt — the four AI quick prompts, detail 'angles | illustration | greek | outline'. Already fired client-side as ai_prompt with a pastor: prefix; it has to reach the server allowlist to be countable.
pastor_source_open — taps on the commentary source line and the All sources sheet. The research names trust-panel visibility against session length as the test.
pastor_file_capture — To sermon taps, detail: reference. Volume per week is the real 'is prep happening here' signal.
pastor_bag_open / pastor_bag_copy — the export step. If copy-all is used, the cross-app integration is worth building; if it is not, it is not.
pastor_preach_handoff — the tap that leaves the PWA. Must fire before window.location.assign, via sendBeacon, or it is lost. Today we have no idea how often he leaves.
pastor_comfort_open — comfort reached from the pastor path. The single most important number in this design, and one no public source will ever supply.
pastor_safety_shown / pastor_safety_dismissed — trigger rate and false positives, which the research names explicitly as the test for this flow.
pastor_week_card_seen / pastor_week_card_dismissed — whether a Sunday-morning retrospective is ever read by a man who is preaching that morning.
reminder_opt_out — by path. The counterweight that stops any nudge change being judged on engagement alone.

D1 / D7 / D30 by path, session length and completion — one dw_events table and one nightly rollup, per the research's first build item. Every claim above is untestable without it, and none of it exists in public data.
self_serve_levers: Live today, no developer: path swatch → Choose your path (change path any time, one tap, saves and opens); campus chip in the Home header; reminder hour and push on/off in More; pastor sign-in and sign-out, which provisions and clears the campus code by itself; starting or stopping a plan from Plans or the wizard; language switch on Home.

Live today for a campus pastor's own congregation: /staff intake — campus corner announcements and Sunday sermon notes, which land in Daily Word's Sermon Notes. This is the estate's real self-serve content mechanism and it already has an approval chain. Any new pastor-editable content should ride it rather than growing a second admin.

Created by this design, no build to change content: public/books/pastor-study.json (en/es/pt/id) holding the Between You & God prompts and the leadership chapter rotation, with the bundled arrays as offline fallback. /books/* is already network-first with cache as offline fallback only, so an edit reaches returning readers on the second open. Ashley edits the file; no rebuild needed for the content itself.
Created by this design, in-app: 'Preaching through' becomes editable in the filed sheet rather than only in a wizard step and a dead screen — the one piece of pastor content that changes weekly.

Named but not built here: an intake action that lets a campus pastor add reflection prompts for their own campus. That is the step that makes the prompt set genuinely self-serve rather than owner-serve, and it needs the intake sign-off chain, so it is an owner decision, not a build step.

Still developer-only after this pass, and honest about it: the Pastors Sermon Prep destination URL, the wizard's plan mappings, the push send window, and the analytics event taxonomy. None of them are content a campus pastor should be editing.

evidence.move: Move prompts and the chapter rotation into /books JSON rather than a new admin
evidence.source: Ruling — /books/* is network-first with cache as offline fallback only (PR #84), and CACHE_NAME/STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION must be bumped together for any sw.js change. That makes /books the one asset class where a content edit reliably reaches returning readers.

open_decisions: Approve the Preach demotion on a deploy preview before it merges. It reorders the opening screen for a persona, which is the same class as the locked look, and the last time an opening screen changed without a preview it was reverted the same night.
Approve the seven rewritten Between You & God prompts. They are about him and about his brothers, in his voice, and no one else should sign them off.

Which crisis lines show for which congregation — US, Australia, New Zealand are drafted — and whether a pastor's own safety moment ever notifies a human. If it does, who: the person a campus pastor would actually accept hearing from, which is not the campus he leads.

Whether the filed captures bag stays a Daily Word sheet or moves wholesale into Pastors Sermon Prep. Two apps holding the same bag is how they end up disagreeing; the copy-all event will tell you which way to go.
Whether push is suppressed for pastors on Sunday morning, and whether Sunday opens are excluded when inferring his reminder hour.
Whether a campus pastor may add campus-specific reflection prompts through /staff intake, which is the step that makes the prompt set genuinely self-serve. The intake approval chain applies.

Whether the Campus Overview prayer number becomes a list he can act on, or stays a count. A number he cannot reach is a scoreboard; a list is pastoral care, and it is a data-access decision, not a design one.
Whether to delete PreachScreen.tsx and SermonWorkspace.tsx now that Preach leaves the app, or keep them parked.
risks: The Preach move reorders the opening screen. Owner-preview-gated by ruling — ship it behind a preview link and do not merge on anyone's word but his.

'Nobody at the church does' must be verified before it ships. Journal rides the user's own cloud row, but that claim has to be checked against user-sync.js column handling and pastor-admin's read scope. If it cannot be proven, the line comes out — an overstated privacy promise to a pastor is worse than no promise.

The filed sheet is a subview-driven card: it must stay mounted with a live open prop and use useSubView alone, never useSubView plus useModalA11y or aria-modal. Both traps have already cost this app a working Android back button and a keyboard-unreachable overlay.

Removing an item from the bag must merge into what is currently in localStorage, never rebuild dw_sermon_prep from React state. A stale mount-time rebuild of a synced dw_* record has already destroyed nine days of another user's progress.

Moving prompts and chapters into /books hits the service-worker cache trap. /books/* is network-first now, but CACHE_NAME, STATIC_CACHE and SW_VERSION must be bumped together, and returning readers see the change on the second open after deploy, not the first.
pastor_preach_handoff fires on a navigation away from the PWA. Without sendBeacon it will never arrive, and the one number that tells you how often he leaves will read zero.
New event types need both the client allowlist and the dashboard aggregation. Adding one without the other silently drops the data.
The two milestone lists — one in streak.ts, one in the greeting section — are already out of sync. Do not add a third list; if the prep line needs a threshold, read the existing one.
Sunday-morning delivery is the weak point of the weekly card. A preaching pastor may never see it. The event will say so within a month; do not defend it if it does not.
Sermon frameworks stay 4D and H.E.A.T. only. Nothing in this design names a framework, and nothing added later should invent one.
Push cannot be verified on a deploy preview or the futures.church proxy — only localhost or production. Any reminder-copy change is verified on prod.
The crisis keyword matcher will produce false positives on scripture. It needs a test suite of biblical phrasing before it goes anywhere near a pastor's screen.
